name: Almond Custard No. 2
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: quarter of a pound of sweet almonds
ingredients.originalText: a quarter of a pound of sweet almonds

ingredients.name: fine white sugar
ingredients.originalText: six ounces of fine white sugar

instructions.text: Blanch a quarter of a pound of sweet almonds
Pound them with six ounces of fine white sugar
Mix them well with the yolks of four eggs
Dissolve one ounce of patent gelatine in one quart of boiling milk
Strain it through a sieve and pour into the mixture
Stir the whole over the fire until it thickens and is smooth
Pour it into your mold and keep it upon ice, or in a cool place, until wanted
When ready to serve dip the mold into warm water, rub it with a cloth and turn out the cream carefully upon your dish

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Blanch a quarter of a pound of sweet almonds
2. Pound them with six ounces of fine white sugar
3. Mix them well with the yolks of four eggs
4. Dissolve one ounce of patent gelatine in one quart of boiling milk
5. Strain it through a sieve and pour into the mixture
6. Stir the whole over the fire until it thickens and is smooth
7. Pour it into your mold and keep it upon ice, or in a cool place, until wanted
8. When ready to serve dip the mold into warm water, rub it with a cloth and turn out the cream carefully upon your dish
